title: Terraform module: private EKS control plane bootstrap & lifecycle (ORBIT)
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Implement a composable Terraform module (ORBIT) to provision and manage Redwood Private EKS control planes. ORBIT will focus on idempotent bootstrap, safe upgrade sequencing, automated health verification, and runbook hooks for on-call operators. The module must work in cross-account VPC setups, integrate with KMS key rotation, and emit structured diagnostics compatible with Console observability.

Goals:
- Provide a single self-contained Terraform module that provisions control plane primitives (IAM roles, control plane endpoint config, VPC endpoints, KMS grants) and lifecycle automation hooks.
- Embed upgrade-safe sequencing primitives (pre-checks, cordon/uncordon helpers, staged config rollouts) so higher-level orchestration can call the module safely.
- Include a health verification layer that runs post-apply checks and reports granular status (API responsiveness, control-plane certificate expiration, etc.).
- Ensure module outputs surface telemetry markers used by Redwood Console for SLA dashboards and canary gating.

Non-goals: the module will not manage worker node pools (handled by separate modules) nor implement full service mesh configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module lives at modules/eks/controlplane-orbit and is covered by CI acceptance tests
Module supports idempotent apply in cross-account VPCs with KMS CMK grants and validates key access
Upgrade flow includes preflight checks and a staged apply flag; a failing preflight aborts the upgrade with clear error codes
Post-apply health probes run automatically and return structured results (ok/warn/error) with reason strings
Console integration: module emits tags/outputs used to correlate runs and exposes a Prometheus metrics endpoint via CloudWatch metrics for control plane lifecycle events
Documentation and runbook created in Confluence with step-by-step rollback instructions and example HCL for canary and fleet upgrades
tasks: Design module schema and variables (networking, kms_key_arn, control_plane_tags, lifecycle_flags)
Implement IAM role/grant patterns for cross-account control-plane provisioning
Implement preflight validation step (Terraform null_resource with local-exec caller) and idempotent marker outputs
Add post-apply health verification (API server ping, endpoint DNS, certificate TTL, audit log sink validation)
Wire CloudWatch metrics + structured CloudWatch Log events for troubleshooting
Add feature flag for staged_rolling_upgrade and example HCL for canary rollout
Write unit and integration CI tests (terraform fmt/validate + k8s API smoke tests using Kind or ephemeral EKS simulator)
Create Confluence docs, sample runbooks, and a demo pipeline in our repo (examples/eks-orbit)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Misconfigured KMS grants could prevent control plane from starting. Mitigation: add explicit preflight that attempts decrypt with the provided key and fail fast with remediation hints.
Risk: Upgrades triggering control-plane downtime. Mitigation: conservative default staged_rolling_upgrade=false; require explicit opt-in; built-in canary recipe with CI gating.

Risk: Terraform state drift when external actors modify control plane. Mitigation: include drift detector null_resource and recommendations for provider-level read-only locks and state locking best practices.
Risk: Operators unfamiliar with new outputs. Mitigation: Console dashboards automatically surface lifecycle events and link to runbook pages.

Risk: Secrets accidentally leaked in logs. Mitigation: redact sensitive fields in post-apply diagnostics and require KMS-encrypted state; update module to honor sensitive=true for outputs where appropriate.

engineering_notes: Prefer explicit resource namespaced prefixes: redwood_orbit_controlplane_* to make state grep easier
Avoid dynamic provider configuration inside module; surface provider inputs and recommend root-level provider aliasing for cross-account use
Use terraform 1.6 features for precondition/postcondition where helpful; fallback to null_resource+local-exec for complex validations
Make health probes pluggable: default AWS-based checks but allow customers to provide custom script hooks
Design outputs for both human-readable summary and machine-readable JSON: controlplane_status, last_preflight, last_health_report
